correctness.rationale: For each singleton, assuming two target atoms in its image makes back lift two disjoint target singletons to intersecting source sets, contradicting forth. Then forth gives \(g[A]\subseteq F(A)\) and back applied to each singleton target contained in \(F(A)\) gives the reverse inclusion. Back from the full source world to the full target world forces onto. Conversely onto atom maps satisfy forth and back by choosing preimages of all target elements with one anchor inside the source. This proves all quantifiers for every positive \(n,m\), including \(n<m\); distinct atom maps give distinct frame maps. Exhaustive independent checks verified all \(826113\) functions for \(n,m\le3\), plus \(852\) induced maps for \(n\le6,m\le3\).
